title: Identifying Lee Collins on a record
summary: Allen plays a record; Humphrey identifies Lee Collins ('Shags') and mentions Robert Thomas.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: I want to play you a record. And I want you to tell me that you know...
Well that Chris, you know he had a tone. You know a round tone. Same as a... You know a... Guy playing this big opera out. But he could... Flips it with that...
That front. Let me put another record out.
He never played no tropics. All small, you know, corners. Great fella he was. We had good battery. Jesse, Cesar, Elisgar, Leroy.
Who's that now? I want you to tell me without looking at it. Who plays trumpet like that? I know he's got your boys on there. I know you recognize him. 된된
That's old Shags. Lee? That's Lee, huh? Lee Collins.

Yeah, that's Lee. Sound like it. You gotta pay some booze, man. Lee Collins. Yeah. That might be Robert Thomas playing some more. He and I played similar like, you know. Oh, I like his playing. Robert. Yeah.
I couldn't bring myself to go see him when he had that chance, I just...
But you know Bill... Bill Stopper with his...
And what is this? You know that chorus, huh? He's imitating somebody, you know. He's not the real man.
